title: Interval-weighted shadow-canary with online bisect hooks and automated rollback choreography
author: Aisha Kaur
release_notes: Adds an interval-weighted canary mode that phases shadow traffic in time windows, integrates an online bisect hook for fast root-cause isolation, and wires automated rollback choreography to existing rollout controllers. Backwards-compatible with existing rollout policies.
description: Motivation: Some production regressions only appear under time-varying traffic mixes or slow-drift signal changes. Existing shadow-canary strategies equally weight mirrored traffic or rely on single-shot percentage ramps which miss temporal signal drift. This PR introduces an 'interval-weighted' shadow-canary mode that: 1) assigns time-windowed weights to mirrored traffic (e.g., higher sampling during high-latency periods), 2) runs targeted lightweight smoke checks per interval, and 3) triggers an online bisect hook that narrows candidate model commits/variants when a metric divergence is detected. The workflow is designed to be safe for Hosted and Dedicated deployments and to integrate with Private installer observability. Changes in this PR: - rollout controller: new IntervalWeightedShadowPolicy type, interval scheduler, and hookpoints for smoke checks and bisect orchestration - prom exporter: interval tagging for metrics and histograms to separate windowed signals - bisect service: a thin coordinator that performs binary narrowing over a small set of candidate model commits using sampled traffic and deterministic replay when necessary - automation: a rollback choreography sequence (quarantine -> snapshot -> staged-revert -> audit-log) wired into existing safety chains - tests: deterministic unit tests for scheduler logic, e2e smoke across a small replica set, and a replay harness for reproducing windowed anomalies Checklist: - [x] Design doc referenced (Linear ENG-4523) - [x] Unit tests added for scheduler and policy parsing - [x] Integration test for smoke-check gating - [x] Metrics tagged and dashboard PR prepared - [x] Rollback choreography implemented and sanity-checked - [x] Security review for audit/logging paths Commits summary and intent: - initial: add IntervalWeightedShadowPolicy and scheduler loop (core rollout controller) - telemetry: add interval tags and counters to prom exporter - bisect: lightweight coordinator implementing halving logic with deterministic replay fallback - automation: implement rollback choreography and tie into controller safety chain - tests: unit + integration + replay harness Changes (high-level file list and snippets): - src/rollout/controller/interval_policy.go (new) - src/rollout/scheduler/interval_scheduler.go (new) - src/telemetry/interval_tags.go (modified) - src/bisect/coordinator.go (new) - infra/playbooks/rollback_choreography.yaml (new) - tests/replay/harness_test.go (new) - web/ui/dashboards/interval_shadow.json (new dashboard metadata) Small illustrative snippet (interval scheduler config parsing): "intervals: [{start: 00:00, end: 06:00, weight: 0.05}, {start: 06:00, end: 18:00, weight: 0.25}, {start: 18:00, end: 24:00, weight: 0.10}]" Review conversation (high-level): - Miguel Rivera (reviewer): "Nice approach; two concerns: 1) bisect could amplify cost if replay falls back often, 2) interval windows need a safety floor for very low traffic windows." - Aisha Kaur (author): "Addressed both: added a hard cap on replay attempts (3) and a min-sampling-floor config (min_weight = 0.01). See latest commits." - Priya Desai: "Tested playback locally, looks stable. Please add observability docs for devs." - Ethan Cole: "Approve after minor rename suggestion for scheduler variable (done)." CI summary: - unit-tests: pass - integration-smoke: pass (flaky test retried once) - lint: pass - e2e-replay: pass Merge outcome: merged into main via squash-merge. Post-merge actions: - dashboard PR merged (web/ui/dashboards/interval_shadow.json) - ops runbook updated and linked in Linear ENG-4523 - notify on-call channel with rollout knobs and min_weight default. Why this is different from existing rollout modes: interval-weighted windows let us target temporal signal variations (daily rhythm, regional peak hours) rather than just percent-sliced cohorts; the bisect hook provides quick isolation of a small set of commits/variants without immediately rolling back globally; the rollback choreography formalizes safe quarantine and snapshot-driven revert so operators can recover with audit evidence. Related: Linear ENG-4523 (design), ENG-4591 (dashboard/telemetry), SUP-1287 (customer-facing incident that motivated min-weight floor).
